title: FloodGuard Billing Desk Guidance: Installments, Payments and the Mortgagee
content:
Billing desk guidance for the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy: when premium is due under each billing plan, how payments and returned payments are applied, what the amount due is, and how the mortgagee is recorded and noticed.

## When premium is billed

- **Annual plan.** A new policy's premium and policy fee are due on the bound date.
- **Two-pay plan.** Half of the premium, rounded half-up to the cent, is due on the bound date with the policy fee; the rest is due six calendar months after the effective date, with the tier's two-pay installment fee.
- **Mortgagee escrow plan.** The premium and policy fee are invoiced to the mortgagee in one invoice due on the effective date.
- **Renewals.** A renewal is billed or invoiced the tier's renewal lead days before expiration and is due on the expiration date; for an escrowed policy the mortgagee on file receives the renewal invoice.

Premium is billed only while the policy is bound, in force or pending cancellation. The status on the policy record decides it, for the policy being billed; a cancelled or expired FloodGuard policy is not billed premium.

*Hypothetical two-pay illustration.* A premium of 1,000.01 USD bound on 10 March with an effective date of 24 March: 500.01 USD (half, 500.005, rounded half-up) is due on 10 March with the policy fee, and the remaining 500.00 USD is due on 24 September with the two-pay installment fee.

## Payments and returned payments

- Payments apply to the oldest charge first.
- A payment is recorded with its confirmation or check number exactly as issued.
- A returned payment reverses the one payment it references, in full, and adds the tier's returned payment fee.

## The amount due

The amount due on a date is the premium installments due on or before that date, plus every fee, returned payment, additional premium and refund posted on or before it, less every payment received and every return premium posted on or before it; it is never less than 0.00.

*Hypothetical example.* On 1 June an account shows a 600.00 USD installment due 1 May, a 75.00 USD policy fee, a 400.00 USD payment and a returned payment of that 400.00 USD with a 25.00 USD fee, all posted before 1 June, and a second installment due 1 July. The amount due on 1 June is 600.00 plus 75.00 plus 400.00 plus 25.00, less 400.00, which is 700.00 USD; the July installment is not yet due and is not counted.

## The mortgagee

- A mortgagee change is recorded only with the mortgagee's name and loan number exactly as on the mortgage statement.
- The mortgagee receives the tier's mortgagee notice period before any cancellation or nonrenewal takes effect.

## Retired clause — no longer in force

The former clause under which a refund was issued only when the premium balance is a credit of at least the tier's refund minimum, to the payer of the most recent payment, so that a credit created by the mortgagee's escrow payment is refunded to the mortgagee, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis for refunds.

superseded_clauses: A refund is issued only when the premium balance is a credit of at least refund_minimum, to the payer of the most recent payment, so a credit created by the mortgagee's escrow payment is refunded to the mortgagee.
